subject: Request: Lumos Retail pilot — HA degrade handling, automated rollback & version pin
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@lumosretail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nicole Huang <nicole.h@lumosretail.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Lumos pilot SLA / failover requirement for BFCM pilot

Hi Monica,

Quick note from the Lumos ops team: our Black Friday pilot windows have tight external SLAs (99.95% availability and 200ms tail latency for checkout flows). Given the traffic burst risk, we need Redwood to authorize an automatic failback mechanism and a short-term version-pin option during the pilot. Specific asks: 

- An automated rollback (canary -> last-known-good) if 1-minute P95 latency exceeds 350ms for two consecutive evaluation windows (5m windows).
- Optional sticky pin for a specific model build for up to 72 hours if degradation is detected and tests show regression.
- Ability for Lumos to trigger immediate manual pin/failover via console+API.

I attached a short requirements doc and the preliminary telemetry thresholds. Can you let me know if Redwood can approve this kind of temporary SLA mitigation and what the escalation path looks like?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Engineering — Lumos Retail
Attachment: lumos_pilot_MVP_requirements.pdf

Looping you in — Lumos (prospect -> pilot customer) is asking for an explicit automatic rollback + temporary version pin for the pilot. They want specific latency triggers and a 72-hr pin window as an option.

Can we draft the policy text we would need to approve, including operational constraints (telemetry windows, safe mode for caching/KV prefixes), Platform API gating, and whether Legal needs a sign-off for temporary SLA carveouts?

I included Rishi for runtime implications and Priyom for orchestration/fallback logic. Aditya/Laura — please advise on what we can commit to without increasing risk to other customers.

Monica

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Lumos pilot SLA / failover requirement for BFCM pilot

Thanks for the ping — quick proposal below we can offer as a pilot-era SLA mitigation. This is intentionally narrow and timeboxed to avoid platform-wide exposure.

Proposed pilot safety policy (summary):
- Trigger windows: continuous 5m evaluation windows, evaluate 1-min P95. If P95 > 350ms for two consecutive windows, mark canary as degraded.
- Automatic action: immediate traffic re-route to the last-known-good model variant (same quantization/replica class) with an API-driven rollback.
- Pin behavior: allow customer-requested pin of a specific model artifact for up to 72 hours. Pin must be requested by a pre-authorized Lumos admin via console or signed HubSpot contact; all pins create an audit entry and temporary telemetry retention flag.
- Safety checks: rollback will only move traffic to variants with matching compatibility metadata (vocab/mesh/tensor shapes). If incompatibility detected, system will fallback to a broader compatible baseline model we maintain for pilot customers.
- Telemetry & guardrails: during pin/pilot, enable enhanced prefix KV caching isolation, increased tokenization tracing for the affected routes, and a circuit-breaker that will revert to region-level routing if errors > 0.5% or anomaly score > 8 for 3m.
- Escalation & SLAs: for the duration of the approved pilot window, Redwood will provide a 4-hour response SLA for rollbacks and a 24-hour postmortem commitment. This is not an SLA change for other customers.

Operational notes: we'll need a signed short-form addendum (two paragraphs) that Lumos acknowledges the temporary pin/rollback as a mitigation, and that they accept the 72-hr pin cap. Legal should be looped for language. Priyom — we can reuse an orchestration policy from INF-4127 but need to add the audit events & pin TTL enforcement. Rishi — what's the risk surface on memory/KV fragmentation when we do frequent rollbacks?

- Aditya

Attachment: rollback_runbook_v2.md
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Lumos pilot SLA / failover requirement for BFCM pilot

Couple of clarifications from the product side before we sign off:

1) Telemetry thresholds: the proposed 350ms P95 trigger seems reasonable for checkout paths, but we should run a short simulation on the pilot sample traffic to estimate false positives. I attached the telemetry thresholds spreadsheet for that.

2) Pin governance: we must require two-person approval for pin requests that originate from Lumos UI unless the request is API-flagged as emergency and comes with an X-Auth token. That prevents accidental long-lived pins.

3) Billing/limits: pins that reduce autoscaling efficiency (e.g., forcing larger models) will be billed at dedicated pilot rates; ops should include estimated delta in the addendum.

If everyone agrees, I'll draft the two-paragraph addendum for Legal and product ops to sign.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
Attachment: telemetry_thresholds.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@lumosretail.com>, Nicole Huang <nicole.h@lumosretail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Lumos pilot SLA / failover requirement for BFCM pilot

Samir / Nicole — thanks for the clear ask and for the requirements doc. We can approve a timeboxed pilot carveout under the following commitments: 

- Redwood will implement the automated rollback and allow customer-requested pinning up to 72 hours during the pilot window (pilot window dates to be confirmed).
- Rollback will trigger on two consecutive 5m windows where 1-min P95 > 350ms; guardrails will be applied as described in Aditya's proposal.
- All pin requests require either a Lumos admin + UI two-person approval or an emergency API token with a signed justification; all pins create immutable audit logs.
- Billing impact: any pin that forces changes increasing unit costs will be charged under the pilot pricing schedule; we will estimate delta after the simulation.
- Next steps: Laura will draft the two-paragraph addendum for signature, Aditya/Priyom will schedule a 1-hour runbook review, and Rishi will run a short traffic simulation to validate thresholds.

Can you confirm the intended pilot dates and provide a list of Lumos pre-authorized admins (names + emails) so Legal can prepare the addendum? Once we have that, we'll put the policy into a short Pilot Operational Agreement and get it signed.

Best,
Monica Patel
Sales Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
